B16C001.summary: In the thirty-sixth year after the great war, Yudhishthira sees many bad omens and hears that the Vrishnis have been wiped out by an iron bolt. Janamejaya asks who brought this about, and Vaishampayana explains that Time drove the clan to ruin through a curse. The curse came after some Vrishni youths tricked visiting sages with Samva disguised as a pregnant woman. This opening sets up the cause of the Yadava downfall, which the rest of the parva describes.

scenes.B16C001S01: Yudhishthira sees omens in the thirty-sixth year and learns of the Vrishni destruction, and Janamejaya asks how and by whose curse it happened.
scenes.B16C001S02: Samva is disguised as a woman and tricks the sages, who curse him to bear an iron bolt, and the king has the bolt ground to powder and bans liquor.

shots.B16C001S01H01: An opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati, and to the word Jaya.
shots.B16C001S01H02: Yudhishthira sees strange omens in the thirty-sixth year, hears of the Vrishni slaughter, and he and his brothers sink into despair.
shots.B16C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks how the Andhakas, Vrishnis and Bhojas came to be destroyed while Vasudeva was still alive.
shots.B16C001S01H04: Vaishampayana says a great calamity fell on the Vrishnis in the thirty-sixth year, and Time drove them to die through the iron bolt.
shots.B16C001S01H05: Janamejaya asks who cursed these heroes and asks for a full account.
shots.B16C001S02H01: Some Vrishni heroes, including Samva, disguise him as a pregnant woman and ask the visiting sages Vishvamitra, Kanwa and Narada about the child.
shots.B16C001S02H02: The sages see through the trick and curse that Samva will bear an iron bolt that destroys the clan, with only Rama and Janardana spared.
shots.B16C001S02H03: Krishna accepts that what is fated will happen. Samva bears the bolt, Ugrasena has it ground to powder and thrown into the sea, and a ban on making liquor is proclaimed under penalty of death.

B16C002.summary: The Vrishnis and Andhakas try to avert their fate, but Time appears in their houses and omens multiply. Animals and nature behave in unnatural ways, and people lose their sense of shame and respect. Krishna sees that the thirty-sixth year has come and that Gandhari's earlier words are about to come true. He orders the clan to make a pilgrimage to the sea-coast, which sets up the final gathering at Prabhasa.

scenes.B16C002S01: A long catalogue of omens and Time's visits to Vrishni houses, followed by Krishna's reading of the signs and his order for a pilgrimage to the sea.

shots.B16C002S01H01: Time appears in Vrishni homes, many unnatural omens follow, and Krishna recognizes the thirty-sixth year and orders the clan to the sea-coast for a pilgrimage.

B16C003.summary: Before leaving, the Vrishni women and men dream of portents, and their weapons and chariots vanish. The clan travels to Prabhasa, where Uddhava departs and the men start a drinking feast. A drunken quarrel between Yuyudhana and Kritavarma leads to Satyaki killing Kritavarma, and a wider brawl breaks out in which Satyaki and Pradyumna die. Krishna picks up a blade of grass that turns into an iron bolt, and the clan destroys itself, with Krishna and Daruka then turning toward Rama.

scenes.B16C003S01: The Vrishnis go to Prabhasa, drink and quarrel, and kill one another in a frenzy, and Krishna and Daruka then set out to find Rama.

shots.B16C003S01H01: Dreams and portents appear, the clan goes to Prabhasa with families and supplies, and the feasting begins there.
shots.B16C003S01H02: Uddhava leaves for his own journey, the men drink heavily at the revels, and Yuyudhana mocks Kritavarma, which Pradyumna applauds.
shots.B16C003S01H03: Kritavarma insults Satyaki by pointing at him and recalling how Satyaki had treated the armless Bhurishrava.
shots.B16C003S01H04: Krishna is angered, Satyaki recalls Kritavarma's wrong against Satrajit, and Satyaki swears to kill him as Draupadi's sons were killed.
shots.B16C003S01H05: Satyaki kills Kritavarma, a brawl spreads, Satyaki and Pradyumna die, and Krishna turns blades of grass into iron bolts that destroy the clan. Daruka and Vabhru then urge Krishna to go to Rama.

B16C004.summary: Krishna sends Daruka to bring Arjuna, then tells Vabhru to guard the women before a hunter's iron bolt kills Vabhru. Krishna goes to find Rama, who has died in yoga and whose serpent soul has gone to the ocean. Krishna thinks over the curses and his own fate, then lies down in yoga, where a hunter named Jara mistakes him for a deer and wounds him. Krishna then ascends to heaven, where the gods honour him.

scenes.B16C004S01: Krishna sends Daruka for Arjuna, has Vabhru guard the women and sees Vabhru killed, visits his father, finds Rama's soul departing as a serpent, and lies down in yoga.
scenes.B16C004S02: The hunter Jara wounds Krishna by mistake, and Krishna rises to heaven and is honoured by the gods.

shots.B16C004S01H01: Krishna and Vabhru find Rama alone under a tree, and Krishna sends Daruka to tell Arjuna of the destruction.
shots.B16C004S01H02: Krishna tells Vabhru to protect the women, Vabhru is killed by a bolt, and Krishna asks Rama to wait for him.
shots.B16C004S01H03: Krishna tells his father to protect the women, says he will go to the forest with Rama, and comforts the grieving women with the promise that Arjuna will come.
shots.B16C004S01H04: In the forest Krishna sees Rama's soul leave his mouth as a white serpent, and the nagas and sacred rivers receive it at the ocean.
shots.B16C004S01H05: Krishna recalls Gandhari's words and Durvasas's earlier words, decides his own time to leave has come, and lies down in yoga.
shots.B16C004S02H01: The hunter Jara shoots Krishna in the heel, mistaking him for a deer. Krishna comforts him and rises to heaven, where the gods and sages welcome him.

B16C005.summary: Daruka reaches the Pandavas and reports that the Vrishnis have destroyed one another. Arjuna sets out for Dwaraka and finds the city empty of its heroes, with the widows and wives of Krishna overcome with grief. Arjuna weeps, is comforted by the women, and then goes on to see his maternal uncle. The scene marks the arrival of the Pandavas' sorrow at the fall of Dwaraka.

scenes.B16C005S01: Daruka brings the news to the Pandavas, Arjuna goes to Dwaraka and finds the city in mourning, and he comforts the women before seeing his uncle.

shots.B16C005S01H01: Daruka tells the Pandavas of the Vrishni deaths, Arjuna goes to Dwaraka and sees the empty city and its grieving women, and he comforts them before going to his uncle.

B16C006.summary: Arjuna finds his uncle Anakadundubhi, who is grieving for his dead sons and kinsmen. The old man tells him how Krishna left before he died, asking Arjuna to take the women and the kingdom and to perform the funeral rites. He says he has stopped eating and will not go on living. The chapter shows Arjuna taking on the responsibility for the surviving Yadavas.

scenes.B16C006S01: Arjuna comes to his uncle, who weeps over the dead and passes on Krishna's last instructions, then announces he will give up his life.

shots.B16C006S01H01: Arjuna bows to his uncle, who is too overcome to greet him in the usual way and weeps for his dead sons and kin.
shots.B16C006S01H02: The uncle speaks of his grief, blames the sages' curse rather than any individual, and relays Krishna's last words: Arjuna should take charge of the women and the kingdom. He says he will starve himself.

B16C007.summary: Arjuna orders the Vrishni survivors to prepare for departure, since the sea will soon swallow Dwaraka. Krishna is cremated with his wives, and the dead Vrishnis are given their rites before the procession leaves the city. On the road, Abhira robbers attack the widows, and Arjuna cannot use his bow or weapons well enough to stop them, losing many women. He settles the rest at new places, and then he goes to see Vyasa, marking the end of the Yadava story for Arjuna.

scenes.B16C007S01: Arjuna prepares the people to leave, Krishna and the dead are cremated, Dwaraka is flooded, the widows are robbed on the road, and Arjuna settles the survivors before visiting Vyasa.

shots.B16C007S01H01: Arjuna tells his uncle that the Earth is unbearable without the Vrishni heroes, orders the citizens to prepare, names Vajra as the new king, and sets a date for leaving.
shots.B16C007S01H02: Krishna dies through yoga, the women mourn in his house, and his body is carried out with ceremony. His wives burn on the pyre, and Arjuna lights it.
shots.B16C007S01H03: Arjuna performs the rites for the slain Vrishnis, cremates Rama and Vasudeva, and leads a large procession of widows and people out of the city.
shots.B16C007S01H04: The sea floods Dwaraka behind them. On the road, Abhira robbers attack, Arjuna's bow and weapons fail him, and many women are taken. He settles the remaining women and people in different places, and some widows burn themselves or go to the forest. Arjuna then goes to Vyasa's retreat.

B16C008.summary: Arjuna visits the hermitage of Vyasa, who notices his despair and asks what has happened. Arjuna describes the Vrishni destruction at Prabhasa, the robbery of the women, his lost strength, and Krishna's departure, and he says he no longer wishes to live. Vyasa explains that all this was fated and that Time governs rise and fall, and that the Pandavas' work is finished. He tells Arjuna that it is time for them all to depart.

scenes.B16C008S01: Arjuna pours out his grief to Vyasa, who explains that the Vrishni fall and Krishna's death were fated and that the Pandavas' task is complete.

shots.B16C008S01H01: Arjuna enters the hermitage of Vyasa and finds him sitting alone.
shots.B16C008S01H02: Arjuna introduces himself and waits. Vyasa welcomes him, asks him to sit, and questions him about possible impurities or defeats that might explain his dejection.
shots.B16C008S01H03: Arjuna recounts the Vrishni slaughter at Prabhasa, the robbery of the women, his failed strength and weapons, and Krishna's departure, and says he does not want to live.
shots.B16C008S01H04: Vyasa consoles him: the destruction was fated and Krishna allowed it, Krishna was the ancient sage who drove Arjuna's chariot, the Pandavas have done their divine work, and it is now time for them to depart.
